Any matrix $A\in \f R^{m\times n}$ of spectral norm 1 and $m\ge n$ can be decomposed as $A=U^\top V$ where
Let $M\in\R^{m\times n}$ with at least one positive entry.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof reduces an arbitrary NP-hard instance PSV(-M), with M in R^{m x n} taken with no restriction on m and n, to a max-angle instance by invoking Theorem th:reduction_SVcones_anglescones. That theorem carries the explicit hypothesis m >= n (inherited from Lemma lem:orthogonal_decomposition), which the proof never verifies; for source instances with m < n the invoked result is applied outside its hypotheses, so the polynomial reduction (and hence NP-hardness of MA(P,Q)) is not established by this argument as written. The conclusion itself remains true: the Cholesky construction in the lemma never uses m >= n (s = rank(A^T A - I) >= n - m automatically gives m + s >= n), or equivalently one may reduce from transposed instances since PSV(-M) and the biclique problem are invariant under transposition.

failure_location.quote: For $A=-M$, $P=\R^m_+$ and $Q=\R^n_+$, Theorem \ref{th:reduction_SVcones_anglescones} says that $\PSV(A,P,Q)$ can be reduced in polynomial time to $\MA(\wt P,\wt Q)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either drop the unneeded hypothesis m >= n from Lemma lem:orthogonal_decomposition and Theorem th:reduction_SVcones_anglescones (the Cholesky-based construction is valid for all m, n, since orthonormality of V forces m + s >= n), or add one line reducing from transposed instances PSV(-M^T).
issues.overall_effect: As written, the proof does not establish the advertised NP-hardness of MA(P,Q) for all pairs of polyhedral cones; it only covers the source instances satisfying m >= n. No other labelled result depends on this corollary.
issues.title: NP-hardness proof of MA invokes the SV-to-MA reduction outside its hypothesis m >= n
issues.why_classification: A routine, local repair (transpose the instance, or remove a hypothesis the proof never uses) restores the corollary with no loss of content and no new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: but it requires that $\langle u, Av\rangle =  \pm  \|A\|$ is not attained for an optimal pair  $(u,v)$ of $\SV(A,P,Q)$.
Then, there exists a solution pair $(u,v)$ of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ where $u$ and $v$ are generators
and the optimal value of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ is the minimum entry of $G^\top A H$.

issues.failure_explanation: The source claims the case <u,Av> = ||A|| (attained at an optimal pair) is 'equivalent' to: both P and Q have only one generator and the 1x1 matrix G^T A H is nonnegative. This equivalence is false. If p = q = 1, the feasible set is the single pair (g_1, h_1), so by the paper's own Proposition pro:nonnegative_case_SVcones the optimal value is the single entry g^T A h, which can be any value in [-||A||, ||A||]; nonnegativity of that entry does not force it to equal ||A||. Counterexample: A = Diag(2,3) in R^{2x2}, P = Q = R_+ e_1 (one unit generator each). Then G^T A H = [2] is a 1x1 nonnegative matrix, yet the optimal value is 2 and not 3 = ||A||, so the stated equivalence fails and the proposed 'easy check' returns a false positive. Only the forward implication (optimal value = ||A|| implies single generators, with entry then equal to ||A|| > 0) is valid; the correct iff requires the entry to equal ||A||, not merely to be nonnegative.

failure_location.quote: However, the case $\langle u, Av\rangle =    \|A\|$ is easy to check, since it is equivalent to say that both $P,Q$ have only one generator and $G^\top AH$ is a $1\times 1$ nonnegative matrix.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition 'G^T A H is a 1x1 nonnegative matrix' by 'the single entry of G^T A H equals ||A||', and add the short Cauchy-Schwarz-equality argument showing that an optimal pair attaining +||A|| forces all generators of each cone to be collinear (hence single generators).
issues.overall_effect: The claimed polynomial-time detection of the extremal case <u,Av> = +||A|| (which, together with the separately treated case -||A||, is what licenses discarding the obstruction to applying Corollary cor:saddle_ConeSV / Property 1 of Theorem th:critical_points_SVcones) is wrong as stated: instances with one generator per cone and 0 < g^T A h < ||A|| would be misclassified as attaining the bound.
issues.title: False equivalence claimed for polynomially checking the case lambda* = +||A||
issues.why_classification: A local, contained repair (strengthen one displayed condition plus a short standard argument) restores the detection procedure; no rate, guarantee, or advertised scope is lost.
